content.familial_criteria: Considered familial when two or more first- or second-degree relatives with HCM or a first-degree relative with autopsy-proven HCM and sudden death at <50 years are detected.
differential_diagnosis: Physiological hypertrophy from intense athletic training
Amyloidosis (consider when increased thickness of interatrial septum, AV valve and/or RV free wall detected)

genetic_counselling_and_testing.indication: Must be offered to all patients with a diagnosis of HCM to identify a possible underlying genetic cause and to all first-degree adult relatives of patients with HCM and a definite disease-causing mutation.
genetic_counselling_and_testing.relatives_evaluation: Clinical evaluation, ECG and echocardiography must be performed in first-degree relatives who have the same definite disease-causing mutation as the index patient. If no definite mutation identified, evaluate relatives and repeat every 2–5 years if non-diagnostic abnormalities are present.

content.minimal_set_of_genes_listed_on_page: TTN, LMNA, MHC, TNNT, Troponin-C, MYPC, RMB20, PLN, Sodium channel alpha unit, BAG3, Actin Alpha Cardiac Muscle, Nexilin, Tropomyosin-1, Vinculin (sarcomeric gene mutations in up to 60% of cases)
content.note_on_sequencing: Additional large-panel sequencing may be considered if clear familial history or structural phenotype, preferably with family segregation.
specific_conditions: Muscular weakness: consider mitochondrial X-linked mutations, glycogen storage disorders, FHLI mutations, Friedreich's ataxia.
Syndromic conditions (cognitive, visual impairment, drooping eyelid): consider mitochondrial X-linked mutations, Noonan syndrome, Danon disease.
Café au lait spots (lentigines): consider Leopard/Noonan syndrome.

endomyocardial_biopsy.indication: May be considered when baseline clinical assessment suggests cardiac inflammation or storage disease not diagnosable by other means.
